title: ProgramKit Development Tools
intent: Allow a fresh Codex or Claude Code session to discover and invoke consumer-owned operations from an explicitly registered ProgramKit-built application through one provider-neutral, byte-verified contract and MCP stdio bridge.
scope: Provider-neutral Development Tool declaration, mapping report, manifest, registration lock, invocation, result, compatibility, and evidence contracts.
Deterministic mapping of every operation in one exact Open Console document, default-all selection, exact-revision exclusions, and blocked-operation reporting.
One neutral MCP 2025-11-25 stdio bridge in Orbyss.ProgramKit.DevelopmentTools.Mcp.
Human-started project-scoped Codex and Claude Code registration lifecycle through the existing program-kit CLI.
Exact local-package-only consumer construction and a minimal test-only generated Console challenge fixture.
Provider-neutral, provider-configuration, genuine Codex, and externally executed genuine Claude Code acceptance evidence.
nonGoals: Corrective Reconstruction, implementation ownership, or clean-room application reconstruction.
Runtime implementation, provider mutation, registration, tool invocation, permission grant, provider call, capability call, or autonomous behavior under design authority.
Remote MCP, provider-native bindings, plugins, instructional skills as transport, or providers beyond Codex and Claude Code.
Package-feed publication, release, deployment, production data, infrastructure, secrets, operational history, or website authority.
assumptions: Open Console remains the authoritative operation document and can evolve independently of the consumer host profile.

The separately approved typed Console implementation has established neutral Open Console ownership and an exact .NET Console binding contract at ce97d8601523b9112207a6a05fd9fb6bb7c56f83 while later typed-host work remains pending; Development Tools binds Open Console and exact consumer bytes rather than dispatcher, binding, or Spectre internals.
Codex and Claude Code continue to support project-scoped local stdio MCP registration under the cited official contracts; every provider work unit rechecks this.
The human can run the genuine Claude Code acceptance proof on another machine from the same exact commit and return unmodified evidence.
The existing private ProgramKit C# gate remains compatible with ProgramKit-owned implementation source.

semanticModels.invariants: Deterministic fixture results may match; provider observations remain labelled; no cross-model behavioral-equivalence claim exists; closure waits for genuine returned Claude Code evidence.

artifactDecisions.requestedOutcome: Represent the exact provider-neutral Development Tool architecture, both reviewed provider integrations, acceptance evidence, and approval boundary as one validated canonical design.

executableBehavior.rationale: The design grants no runtime execution, package preparation, registration, configuration mutation, provider start, trust, permission, or invocation authority.

valueLifecycle.rationale: Canonical bytes are schema-validated, semantically checked, digest-bound by Planning 3.0 and the review manifest, and rechecked at approved work-unit boundaries.

agentRetrieval.rationale: The review set is explicit repository input; no agent retrieval, instructional skill, plugin, or provider wrapper is created.

agentProcedure.rationale: MCP and provider integration are prospective product work units, not active capabilities or autonomous procedures.

humanCommunication.audience: The human ProgramKit reviewer, later bounded implementer, and external Claude Code acceptance operator.
humanCommunication.decisionAuthorityBoundary: Only explicit human approval of this review-set version and exact canonical design and plan SHA-256 values authorizes implementation.
humanCommunication.rationale: Canonical JSON, concise projections, fixtures, evidence, compatibility matrix, validation report, and manifest expose the exact architecture and proof obligations.

governance.provenancePolicy: Exact converged human intent and ProgramKit source commit ce97d8601523b9112207a6a05fd9fb6bb7c56f83 are named; current implemented and approved-prospective Console source truth is separated.
governance.digestPolicy: The review manifest and Planning 3.0 plan bind exact canonical bytes; material change requires revalidation, new digests, and renewed explicit approval.
governance.compatibilityPolicy: Contracts, schemas, packages, executable bytes, Open Console revisions, selected operations, MCP revision, provider configuration, locks, CLI grammar, diagnostics, and evidence version explicitly.
governance.migrationPolicy: Every change requires an explicit update proposal; incompatible change requires reviewed migration or exact removal and fresh registration.

dataHandling.redactionPolicy: Artifacts contain identities, paths, versions, digests, normalized configuration, and outcomes only; command values, input/output values, environment values, credentials, and secret values are excluded from durable evidence.
dataHandling.externalizationPolicy: Canonical contracts and documentation remain ProgramKit-owned. Provider project entries and consumer manifests are exact governed projections with separate ownership locks.
dataHandling.ephemeralDataPolicy: Provider sessions, MCP/consumer processes, invocation values, environment values, and transient approval prompts are observations, not durable design content.

artifactDecisions.rationale: One schema-governed canonical design keeps reusable mechanics, provider configuration, human authority, and external evidence distinct while all runtime work remains blocked pending exact approval.

security.policy: Deny filesystem, network, and secret access by default; verify exact locked bytes before discovery and invocation.
guarantees: Positive declarations bind exact filesystem roots, network destinations, and provider-owned secret references.
Input and output validate against exact schemas.
Tamper, incompatibility, collision, path escape, and unowned configuration fail before partial mutation or process start.
exclusions: No sandbox escape, credential storage, secret value recording, broad environment capture, or permission grant.

authority.policy: Selection, proposal, registration, provider trust/permission, and invocation are separate human/provider authority transitions.
guarantees: Provider mutation requires explicit acceptance of one exact proposal digest.
The human starts each provider session and owns trust/server approval.
The provider owns permission evaluation for each actual tool call.
exclusions: No self-registration, self-permission, provider start, AI/provider call, capability call, nested invocation, or autonomous loop.

secrets.policy: Secrets are denied by default and may be referenced only by name through a positively declared provider-owned source.
guarantees: Secret values never enter declarations, manifests, locks, registration commands, stdout, diagnostics, or evidence.
exclusions: No secret value discovery, persistence, redaction guesswork, or transmission beyond the exact consumer access boundary.

persistence.policy: Persist canonical artifacts, locally prepared packages, one owned project configuration entry, and one provider-specific ownership lock.
guarantees: Writes are atomic and project-contained.
Unrelated provider configuration bytes are preserved.
Removal deletes only exact owned state.
exclusions: No user/global provider configuration, runtime process state, invocation values, or provider trust/permission claims.

failure.policy: Fail closed with stable classifications and no partial mutation when required identity, compatibility, policy, byte, path, provider, or ownership evidence is absent or changed.
guarantees: Selected incompatible operations are reported as blocked.
Provider drift, collision, tamper, incompatible versions, and uncontained paths block.
Timeout kill is provider/bridge evidence and never fabricated as a consumer exit code.
exclusions: No silent omission, fallback transport, automatic retry, auto-upgrade, partial registration, or inferred success.

concurrency.policy: Each operation declares maximum concurrency; the safe default and proof fixture use one.
guarantees: The bridge refuses calls above the declaration and starts a fresh consumer process for each accepted call.
exclusions: No shared consumer process, unbounded queue, automatic retry, or implicit parallelism.

cancellation.policy: Advertise and translate cancellation only for explicitly supporting operations; enforce bounded timeout independently.
guarantees: Cancellation races have explicit outcomes.
Cancellation makes no rollback or idempotency claim.
The lower applicable declared/provider timeout is enforced.
exclusions: No claim that a cancelled or killed consumer reversed side effects.

observability.policy: Record exact identities, versions, digests, state transitions, provider versions, trust/permission observations, process boundaries, and canonical result digests.
guarantees: Provider-neutral and provider-specific evidence are separate and schema-bound.
Session A, B, and C isolation is observable.
Cross-provider closure records genuine external Claude Code evidence or remains open.
exclusions: No prompts, reasoning traces, raw inputs/outputs, environment values, credentials, secret values, or unsupported equivalence claims.

compatibility.policy: Pin exact versions and digests; require explicit review and update for every change, including compatible additions.
guarantees: ProgramKit packages are 0.1.0-alpha.1, contracts/schemas are 1.0.0, and MCP is 2025-11-25 for v1.
New Open Console operations cannot enter existing registration silently.
Incompatible change requires a reviewed migration or exact remove and fresh registration.
exclusions: No floating versions, silent upgrades, inferred provider compatibility, build-output identity, or unreviewed migration.

scenarios.intent: Construct an exact Development Tool manifest from a ProgramKit-built Console application.
preconditions: Exact locally prepared ProgramKit packages and controlled source mapping exist.
The Open Console document, consumer package/executable, declaration, and output schemas are exact.
Every selected operation has a complete access and side-effect policy.
steps: Map and report every Open Console operation.
Default-select all operations and apply exact-revision exclusions.
Block any selected operation that cannot be projected safely.
Derive structured inputs and canonical Console invocation mappings.
Emit and verify one canonical manifest binding every exact byte.
outcomes: Every operation is selected, explicitly excluded, or selected-but-blocked.
Repeated construction from identical inputs is byte-identical.
No provider registration, permission, or invocation occurs.
failureOutcomes: Ambiguous, non-JSON, interactive, unbounded, unclassified, changed, or incompatible operations block.
Project/source/build-output coupling or uncontrolled ProgramKit source mapping rejects the consumer.

scenarios.intent: Register exact tool bytes and invoke a consumer operation through a fresh provider session.
preconditions: A verified manifest, neutral bridge package/executable, provider evidence, and clean project configuration exist.
The human has reviewed the deterministic proposal and starts the exact register command with its digest.
steps: Verify every proposal input and refuse collisions.
Atomically write only the owned provider entry and provider-specific lock.
End session A with no surviving process.
Start a cold session B and supply only semantic intent.
Let the provider discover the bridge, apply trust/permission, and call one operation.
Verify input, start one fresh consumer process, validate the canonical result, and record redacted evidence.
outcomes: Discovery depends solely on persisted provider project registration.
The exact registered bridge and consumer bytes execute.
The result and evidence conform without an autonomous loop.
failureOutcomes: Tamper, drift, collision, denied permission, timeout, concurrency, or policy violation fails closed.
The registration writer or bridge never compensates by granting permission or changing provider state.

scenarios.intent: Review exact change and explicitly update or remove one owned registration.
preconditions: The lock and current owned provider entry verify exactly.
An update proposal reports all added, removed, and changed operations.
steps: Read status without mutation.
Verify old state and exact new inputs.
Require explicit acceptance of the update proposal digest or exact remove command.
Atomically replace the owned entry and lock, or remove only them.
Start cold session C after removal.
outcomes: The removed tool is not discoverable in session C.
failureOutcomes: Changed, missing, colliding, incompatible, or unowned state refuses mutation.
No rollback, cleanup, or configuration adoption is inferred.

scenarios.actor: ProgramKit reviewer and external Claude Code operator
scenarios.intent: Prove the same exact neutral artifacts through genuine Codex and Claude Code cold sessions.
preconditions: Codex evidence is genuine and complete.
The human can reproduce the exact commit and artifacts on the Claude Code machine.
steps: Run Claude sessions A, B, and C without inherited process or command knowledge.
Return provider-labelled evidence without secret or invocation values.
Validate every shared and Claude-specific digest and observation in ProgramKit.
Close acceptance only when every required proof and negative case passes.
outcomes: The same canonical fixture result and neutral artifact digests are proven for both providers.
Provider-specific trust, permission, version, and configuration observations remain distinct.
failureOutcomes: Missing, fabricated, changed, or non-cold Claude evidence leaves cross-provider acceptance open.
No behavioral-equivalence claim is made beyond tested deterministic contracts.

statusClaims.claim: The replacement review design exists from explicit converged human intent; no runtime, registration, provider, permission, capability, or acceptance implementation is claimed.
